e.etymology: A variant of Axton, a surname-style name that rose in the 2010s alongside Axel and Paxton.
A respelling of Blakely, an English surname and place name from Old English blaec, dark, and leah, a woodland clearing.
A respelling of Reign, the English word for a monarch's rule, from Latin regnum, kingdom. Reign became a given name in the 2010s.
Best known from playwright Katori Hall, creator of the TV drama P-Valley. Katori is also a Japanese place name and surname.
namesakes: Katori Hall (Pulitzer-winning playwright, creator of P-Valley)

e.etymology: A respelling of Niko or Nico, short forms of Nicholas, from Greek Nikolaos, formed from nike, victory, and laos, people.
A Breton name, borne by a legendary saint and linked through Honorine to Latin honor. In early 1900s America it was more likely a variant of Elnora or Lenora.
A short form of Campbell, the Scottish clan name from Gaelic cam beul, crooked mouth. Camp is also an English surname and an outdoorsy word name.
A respelling of Nalani, a Hawaiian name from na lani, the heavens or the chiefs. The added h follows spellings like Kehlani and Nahla.
The Latin spelling of Greek Ikaros, the son of the craftsman Daedalus. Escaping Crete on wings of feathers and wax, he flew too near the sun and fell into the sea. The name's meaning is unknown.

assoc.t: Greek myth figure who flew too close to the sun

e.note: Icarus is a byword for fatal overreach: in the myth he ignores his father's warning and falls to his death.

e.etymology: A spelling of Kashvi, a modern Indian name built on the Sanskrit root kash, to shine, the same root as Kashi, the old name of Varanasi.
A short form of Xochitl, the Nahuatl (Aztec) word for flower, long used as a girls' name in Mexico.
A pet form of Rivka, the Hebrew form of Rebecca, and in recent American use also a short form of River.
A modern American blend of Kai with the ending of Naomi or Kiyomi.
The Ethiopian and Eritrean form of Jehoaddan, in the Bible the mother of King Amaziah of Judah. The Hebrew name joins the name of God to a word for delight.
A one-n spelling of Jennifer, the Cornish form of Guinevere, Welsh Gwenhwyfar, from gwen, white or fair, and a word for a phantom or spirit. This spelling is common in Latin America.
In older American records a spelling of Daniel, from Hebrew Daniyyel, God is my judge. It is also the usual English spelling of the Arabic, Persian and Malay form, Daniyal.
A combination of Rose and Anne, a variant of Rosanne. Rose is the flower name; Anne comes from Hebrew Hannah, grace.
namesakes: Roseanne Barr (comedian and star of the sitcom Roseanne)
Roseanne Roseannadanna (Gilda Radner's Saturday Night Live character)

assoc.t: Roseanne Barr and her ABC sitcom Roseanne

e.etymology: A variant of Reuben, from Hebrew Re'uven, behold, a son, the name of Jacob's eldest son. Rubin is also a Jewish surname.
namesakes: Rubin Carter (boxer known as Hurricane, freed after a wrongful murder conviction)

e.etymology: A surname-style name of the early 1900s, shaped like Dalton, Elton and Melton and probably read as the town in the dell.
A spelling of Darian, a modern name that grew out of Darius, Old Persian for he who holds firm the good, with the sound of Darren and Adrian.
In the US mostly a modern spelling in the Kalen and Kaelin family. Kalin is also a Bulgarian boys' name, the masculine of Kalina, the viburnum shrub.
The Latin feminine of Stephanus, from Greek stephanos, a crown or garland, the victor's wreath. Stephanie is the French form of the same name.
A spelling of Jaclyn, the American short form of Jacqueline, the French feminine of Jacques. Jacques is the French form of Jacob and James.
From the English surname for someone who lived by a notable rock, and from the word itself. It is also the English form of the saint's name Roch or Rocco.
namesakes: Rock Hudson (leading man of 1950s and 1960s Hollywood)

assoc.t: The Rock, wrestling name of Dwayne Johnson

e.etymology: From the English occupational surname for a summoner, the officer who called people to court. American use honored Charles Sumner, the abolitionist senator from Massachusetts.
namesakes: Sumner Redstone (media mogul who controlled Viacom and CBS)

e.etymology: In the US mostly a modern coinage close to Janiya and Janae. Janya is also an Indian name from Sanskrit janya, born or produced.
From Greek eu, good, and doron, gift. In Greek myth Eudora is the name of several sea and rain nymphs.

e.meaning: victory of the people; young pup
e.etymology: A respelling of Colin, which has two sources: a medieval pet form of Nicholas, victory of the people, and the Scottish Gaelic name Cailean, young pup.
